findings.title: Windows archive member names escape the restore staging directory
findings.summary: Overwrite or create arbitrary files writable by the user outside the chosen restore target, potentially including configuration or startup paths.

severity.rationale: Direct source, validation, and attack-path evidence support the calibrated local impact.

taxonomy.category: Path traversal or resource boundary failure

findings.remediation: Manifest exact-name, CRC, size and SHA-256 checks prove archive consistency but not Windows destination containment. target_root nonexistence and final os.replace occur after the out-of-tree write.

codeEvidence.label: Uncontained operation
codeEvidence.code: # operation consumes the value without the required shared proof
codeEvidence.explanation: The value reaches the security-relevant sink without containment or identity validation.

rootCause.summary: _safe_member_path uses PurePosixPath and rejects only POSIX absolute paths and an independent '..' part; restore joins those accepted parts into a Windows Path and opens it for writing without resolving and proving containment under staging.

validation.method: static source trace and focused validation
validation.summary: Path('C:/stage').joinpath(*PurePosixPath(r'\Windows\Temp\owned').parts) resolves as a rooted Windows path; UNC and D: forms similarly discard the staging root. No resolved containment check precedes destination.open('wb').
limitations: No live or external target was used.

attackPath.summary: Arbitrary Windows file write with the restoring user's authority.

remediationTests: Reject escape, wrong identity, root-equal, and over-budget inputs before side effects.
Run the original candidate regression under a temporary workspace.
preventiveControls: Centralize safe path, identity, and archive-budget validation.
